prompt: Explain eventual consistency in exactly three bullet points.
text:
# Eventual Consistency

• **Delayed Synchronization**: Data updates are not immediately reflected across all system copies. Instead, changes propagate asynchronously over time, allowing different nodes to temporarily have different versions of the same data.

• **High Availability Trade-off**: The system prioritizes availability and partition tolerance over immediate consistency, enabling it to remain responsive even when network failures occur or nodes are unreachable.

• **Guaranteed Convergence**: Given enough time with no new updates, all nodes will eventually sync and agree on the same final state, ensuring data integrity despite temporary inconsistencies.
